why_rejected: The official signed-monotonic closure got worse on Z (5 mm -> 0 mm) because the +5 mm grid point drew one descent-corridor rejection and one single-sided contact -- two independent, roughly 1-in-6 events landing on the same point -- and the closure truncates at the first failing magnitude. Total Z reliability was statistically unchanged (15/27 vs 16/27). Adopting 118 mm would therefore trade the committed acceptance basis for a noise draw.
protocol_finding: At the measured ~65 % per-trial reliability a 3-repetition, 9-point signed-monotonic closure reports an envelope of >=10 mm only 18-27 % of the time. The reported number moved opposite to a demonstrated physical improvement, so the measurement protocol -- not the hardware -- is the limiting instrument. Strengthening it (more repetitions, or separating ADR-0016 section 3 descent-corridor admission from grasp tolerance as that section already requires) is an ADR-level decision and is not taken here.
truth_boundary: Simulator truth supplied only the calibration-only target initialization. Contact, broker, and attach evidence came from the production path.
